title.narrative: National stakeholders engaged to support the resetting of Local Multiparty Governance Reform agenda
Communique/statement/minutes on the consultations affirming support for the proposals for the LMPG reforms

target.value: 1.1 A National consensus conference on the proposals for the establishment of LMPG system organised and a national compact adopted at the 30th anniversary commemoration of the 1992 constitution. 1.2 The legal processes involving Parliament for amending articles 55(3) and 243(1) triggered and public education on the proposed reforms embarked upon for a successful implementation of the local government reforms.

actual.value: Although most of the activities were successfully implemented, the national consultative conference which was to climax the consultations with relevant stakeholders did not take place. Due to the political and economic developments at the time, the national conference was not held. Nevertheless, IDEG engaged the President in April 2022 where he affirmed his commitment in the process and provided direction for the Constitutional Amendment agenda. The outcome of this meeting was the speech delivered by the President on 28th April 2022 to mark 30th Anniversary of the referendum that approved the 1992 Constitution. The President in his speech, prioritized the reform of the current local government system by amending Article 55(3) and made building a broad-based consensus a precondition for him to relaunch the legal process for amending the relevant.

target.value: Major political parties support and include the resetting the LMPG reforms agenda

actual.value: The 2 main political parties, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) and the New Patriotic Party (NPP) both include LG reforms in their 2020 Election Manifestos

target.value: 1.1 More consultations with National stakeholders and leaders towards a national consensus conference in 2022 on the LMPG reforms agenda. 1.2 Working in close collaboration with the Ministry of Local Government Decentralization and Rural Development and allied CSOs to build the needed stakeholders’ consensus on reforming the local governance and the multiparty democratic system in Ghana

actual.value: The key result achieved was the emergence of consensus among the key stakeholders on the priorities for reforms: (i) Parliament should adopt and publish the Constitutional Review Implementation Committee Report (CRIC) which was submitted in 2014.; (ii) Pursue the limited amendment of the Constitution [(Articles 55 (3) and 243)] which is the interest of the President. (iii) Commission an independent body the Multiparty Democracy and Constitutional Review Commission (MDCRC) and the Constitutional Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee of Parliament to handle the remaining constitutional articles for deliberations and subsequent implementation. This bi-partisan group of experts would ensure an incremental amendment of the remaining articles in the CRIC report

title.narrative: The constitutional amendment of Articles 55(3) and 243(1) is reinitiated
Consensus built on amendment of Articles 55 (3) and 243 (1) and Government announces decision to reinitiate Constitutional Amendment process.

target.value: More consultations with National stakeholders and leaders towards a national consensus conference in 2022 on the LMPG reforms agenda

actual.value: IDEG adopted a strategy of sensitizing the leadership of key stakeholder groups, and then supporting them to engage their membership during their own scheduled meetings. This has fostered more efficient use of time and resources and while this did not lead to the expected schedule of activities, it nevertheless ensured wider consultations and fostered an environment for acceptance.

target.value: National consensus and ownership of the constitutional amendment achieved and the process for the reforms re-initiated

actual.value: The National Conference was not held as agreed due to the prevailing economic and political situation at the time.
